summary: Backend-only regression on POST/GET /api/inquiries with fail-safe alerts. Ran 10 pytest cases against public REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL — all 10 passed. Verified graceful degradation when RESEND/TWILIO env vars are empty: submission returns 200 immediately (<3s), no exceptions in backend logs, alerts are no-op via early return in _send_email_alert/_send_whatsapp_alert. Verified no Mongo _id leakage on list/get. Verified 422 on invalid email and missing required fields. Verified 404 on unknown id. Verified list is sorted newest-first.
critical_code_review_comments: Consider capping list_inquiries pagination — currently returns up to 1000 with no limit/offset params. Not blocking now but will become an issue at scale.

asyncio.create_task(send_alerts(...)) result is not awaited/tracked; unhandled task exceptions are logged inside send_alerts (good), but there is no supervision if event loop shuts down mid-flight. Acceptable for fire-and-forget MVP.

created_at is stored as ISO string but declared as datetime in Pydantic model — works via fromisoformat re-parse on read paths, but consistent storage as BSON datetime would simplify sorting/filtering later.
Reused module-level `client` name in _send_whatsapp_alert shadows the Motor Mongo client at function scope only — safe but confusing; rename to twilio_client.
seed_data_creation: Test inquiries prefixed with TEST_ created via API (persisted in Mongo). Not cleaned up — safe as identifiable test data.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run tests serially: `pytest /app/backend/tests/test_inquiries.py -n 0 -v` — the pytest.ini enables xdist by default and cross-worker state (pytest.created_id) breaks the list/get tests if parallel. If you need parallel, refactor to persist created id via a shared file or a session-scoped fixture returning the id.
rca of the issue: N/A — no issues found. Feature works as designed: alert functions early-return when env vars empty; asyncio.create_task ensures non-blocking; try/except in send_alerts wrapper prevents any provider exception from propagating.
